findings.detail: Important, below Critical; reported under the explicit production budget/deadline exception. Allocation publication and parent-state inspection happen before the call's deadline becomes active. If another process holds the shared audit lock for six seconds during allocation of a five-second fingerprint call, these operations wait using the independent 15-second IO limit, exceeding the inclusive call limit before execution starts. Once the lock becomes available, validation checks only recorded deadline relationships, so execution can still reach Popen after the allocation has expired. Apply the call's deadline to allocation publication and parent-state reads.
findings.evidence: command() calls runtime.allocate() and runtime.states() at checked_core.py:223-225, then installs ACTIVE_DEADLINE at line 227. allocate() establishes started_at and deadline at lines 634-642 but writes the allocated record at line 646 without activating that deadline. states() also acquires its lock without an explicit deadline at lines 661-662. With no active deadline, regular_file() selects deadline_after(IO_LIMIT), 15 seconds, at lines 106-109. pipeline_command() shares the allocation path at line 1277. _command() reaches Popen at line 261 without an elapsed-deadline check.
findings.title: Boundary arithmetic: audit lock waits escape the call's inclusive limit
